item1_text: Callout Example 2 In November 2024, the Correctional Service of Canada data transfer indicates that the client was released from incarceration in October 2024. A review of the Department's systems confirms that the client was in receipt of the OAS pension and the GIS before their incarceration, but they have not yet advised the Department of their release. The client has a spouse who has been receiving the ALW benefit based on their individual income as the rate is to their advantage while the pensioner was incarcerated. The ALW benefit is reverted to being calculated on the couple’s combined income effective October 2024. Since the account is being adjusted in November 2024, an overpayment for the month of October 2024 is established. The pensioner’s account remains suspended and is placed on hold for 30 days awaiting written notification of their release. On November 30, 2024, the written notification of release is received from the client and the release date provided is confirmed as a match with the Correctional Service of Canada data transfer. The client's OAS pension and GIS account is reviewed and they continue to be eligible to receive the OAS pension and the GIS . The benefits are reinstated effective October 2024, the month of their release from incarceration.
item2_text: Callout Example 2 The client was incarcerated on November 12, 2020, and was released from incarceration on July 5, 2024. The incarceration dates were confirmed with the Correctional Service of Canada data transfer. The client turned 65 on November 16, 2022. On August 12, 2024, after being released from incarceration, the client applied for their OAS pension and the GIS . The client is not entitled to the GIS as their income is in excess. They have provided the following residence history: Birth to May 31, 1993: Italy June 1, 1993 to present: Canada In normal circumstances, the client would receive a choice between: 31/40ths effective July 2024; or 29/40ths with 19 months of actuarial adjustment effective July 2024. Since this client was incarcerated before their 65th birthday, the residence can accumulate up until the month the pension is approved. However, the client is not entitled to accrue an actuarial adjustment for the months they were incarcerated. Therefore, in this situation, no pension choices would be offered to the client. Their pension would be approved effective July 2024 at a rate of 31/40ths.

In the November 2024 accounting month, the account must be suspended.
item2_text: Callout Example 2 In November 2024, the Correctional Service of Canada data transfer indicates that the client was released from incarceration in October 2024. A review of the Department's systems confirms that the client was in receipt of the OAS pension and the GIS before their incarceration, but they have not yet advised the Department of their release. The client has a spouse who has been receiving the ALW benefit based on their individual income as the rate is to their advantage while the pensioner was incarcerated. The ALW benefit is reverted to being calculated on the couple’s combined income effective October 2024. Since the account is being adjusted in November 2024, an overpayment for the month of October 2024 is established. The pensioner’s account remains suspended and is placed on hold for 30 days awaiting written notification of their release. On November 30, 2024, the written notification of release is received from the client and the release date provided is confirmed as a match with the Correctional Service of Canada data transfer. The client's OAS pension and GIS account is reviewed and they continue to be eligible to receive the OAS pension and the GIS . The benefits are reinstated effective October 2024, the month of their release from incarceration.

item1_text: Callout Semi-monthly proration formula (Semi-monthly amount of the benefit × 2 × number of months received from the effective month of the option to the end of calendar year ÷ number of months from the effective month of the option to end of calendar year) × 12
item2_text: Callout Example 2 The client retired on October 4, 2020. The client received their first EI benefits payment of $100.00 on November 5, 2020 for the period of October 25 to 31. The client received their final payment on February 10, 2021 for the week of January 31 to February 6, 2021. Determine the number of full weeks from the effective date (November 1) to the end of the calendar year (December 31): 9 weeks Note: The calculation is based on full weeks only. If a partial week remains after counting all full weeks, consider it as one full week. Prorate the EI benefits using the formula: ($100.00 × 9) ∕ 2 × 12 = $5,400.00 Calculate the maximum possible yearly amount: $100.00 × 52 = $5,200.00 Compare the results of Step 1 and Step 2 to determine the lesser amount: In this case, you must use the lesser amount of $5,200.00 from Step 2. Note: EI benefits are paid bi-weekly, but a weekly rate is used by EI to determine how much the client will receive on their payment. Therefore, the calculation to prorate a weekly benefit is used for a current year option.
